prose.standard-how.say: How to write anything a customer reads.

prose.standard-reader.say: Write for a reader who is not technical and has to decide what to do, the way a knowledgeable person talks to a colleague: plain English, short, active voice, each point once and every sentence earning its place.

prose.standard-names.say: Write files, commands and package names as they are, name everything else by what it does, explain a technical name in the same sentence, and invent no terms.

prose.standard-risk.say: Say what is at risk, what fixes it and what happens if it is left.

prose.standard-facts.say: Give facts and let the reader weigh them.

prose.standard-length.say: Vary sentence length, and let a sentence carry its reason in a clause.

prose.standard-never.say: Never write an em or en dash, a semicolon, antithesis in any form such as "it isn't X, it's Y", "X rather than Y", "X instead of Y" or "not only X but also Y", a cleft sentence such as "it is X that", a trailing which clause, an "X, being Y" appositive, passive voice, a double negative, an opener that fills, signposts or announces, a closing summary, a metaphor or flourish, spatial framing of an abstract thing, commentary on why something matters, a "what" clause standing in for a name, two sentences in a row opening on the same word, more than one short sentence in a paragraph, or a point made twice.

prose.standard-words.say: Use the common word: never "furthermore", "moreover", "robust", "seamless", "leverage", "crucial", "navigate", "landscape", "delve", "tapestry", "accrue" or "warrant".
